commits.message:
feat(review,accuracy): let reviewers correct fields inline, and turn that signal into a field-level accuracy dashboard

Direct answer to "are we getting real accuracy and visibility": before
this, the internal Hermes review page could only Publish, Reject,
Reclassify, or Delete a draft -- there was no way to fix a single wrong
field. A draft that was 90% correct with one bad field forced a choice
between publishing it wrong or throwing away the other 90%. That's both
an efficiency problem (every fixable draft either gets published wrong
or wastes a mostly-good parse) and the reason there was no accuracy data
at all: the only place a human correction was ever captured was the
claim-and-verify flow (a recruiter fixing a field via their claim link),
which is a small fraction of drafts. Whatever a reviewer manually
double-checked and worked around never left a trace anywhere.

Turns out the accuracy half of this was already designed and half-built:
record_recruiter_correction (app/email_parsing/provenance.py) already
existed with a docstring describing exactly this -- "compare extractor
output against extractor='recruiter_correction' rows ... and you know
which fields the parser gets wrong" -- but nothing ever read that data
back out. This closes that loop from both ends: a second correction
source (reviewers, not just recruiters), and the actual accuracy reader
that was always the plan.

Inline field editing (app/drafts/service.py: apply_field_corrections,
PATCH /drafts/{id}/fields in app/routers/drafts.py): a reviewer can edit
any of the fields already shown as rows on the review page -- job_title,
company, location, rate_or_salary, employment_type, work_authorization,
years_of_experience, required_skills, preferred_skills, linkedin_url for
requirements; the equivalent set for each hotlist consultant record.
job_description is deliberately not editable -- it's free-text prose in
its own collapsible section, not a labeled field row, and editing prose
isn't what this loop is for. Every actual value change is recorded via
the new record_reviewer_correction (mirrors record_recruiter_correction
exactly, distinct extractor value so the dashboard can show which
channel is catching errors) before the payload is saved, so correction
history survives independently of whatever the field gets edited to
next. Silently drops any submitted field not in the editable set rather
than erroring, so a stray extra key in a request never fails the whole
save.

Field-level accuracy (app/drafts/accuracy.py, GET /accuracy/summary):
computed from field_provenance, not a hand-labeled test corpus -- reuses
the real, continuously-growing signal that reviewer edits and recruiter
claim corrections already produce as a side effect of normal work.
Two numbers per field, not one, because they answer different
questions and conflating them was the obvious way to get this wrong:

- fill_rate: of every draft Hermes saw, in what share did it produce a
  non-empty value for this field at all (recall).
- precision: of the values it DID produce, what share did a human leave
  untouched (correctness). Computed by inspecting each correction's own
  "before" value: if the field was empty before the correction, that's
  a fill_rate story (a gap got filled in), not a precision miss, and is
  excluded from the precision denominator entirely -- otherwise a field
  Hermes correctly leaves blank half the time would look like it has
  terrible precision purely because of the other half.

Fields with fewer than 10 samples in the selected window are flagged
`reliable: false` rather than shown as a confident-looking percentage
from 1-2 data points -- the dashboard visibly marks these "low sample"
instead of hiding the number, since a reviewer should be able to see a
field is still building up data rather than wonder why it's missing.

Frontend: FieldRow (app/components/FieldRow.tsx) gained an inline edit
affordance -- click Edit, change the value (comma-separated for skill-
array fields, numeric-coerced for years-of-experience), Save or Cancel,
wired on both the job-requirement Card and each hotlist consultant's
Card in DraftDetailPage. New AccuracyPage.tsx: a 7/30/90-day range
picker, two field tables (job requirement / hotlist) sorted worst-
precision-first so the most actionable row is always on top, a color-
coded precision bar, and a "worst field" callout banner. Reachable from
top nav alongside the existing "Blocklist & taxonomy" link.

New coverage: scripts/hermes-950-review-accuracy-check.py -- applying a
correction updates and persists the payload; non-editable fields
(job_description) are silently ignored rather than erroring; submitting
an unchanged value is a safe no-op; the accuracy summary correctly
separates a "filled a gap" correction from a "fixed a wrong value"
correction using two drafts with different starting states; small-
sample fields are flagged unreliable. Full regression suite (18 checks
now) green against a freshly built image and freshly reset schema.
Frontend type-checks and builds clean.

No new tables -- this is built entirely on the existing drafts and
field_provenance tables, which is also why it required no schema
migration and works immediately against the drafts already sitting in
the review queue.
